waves.name: Setup utilities and CICS file fences
waves.rationale: Jobs that run no application program and share no dataset the graph can see. Two of them, CLOSEFIL and OPENFIL, are the CEMT fences that every wave 5 posting and refresh run needs, and they work unchanged on the mainframe until then. The rest are one time setup (CBADMCDJ defines CICS resources, DEFCUST and ESDSRRDS build clusters no program reads) or demos (FTPJCLS, LISTFILS, RACFCMDS). This wave carries no business logic, so it does not prove the port toolchain. It meets the deploy, rollback and test conditions but not the fourth: no business stakeholder can name what it delivers. Treat it as a chore, most of it retirement.
waves.unblocks: Nothing on its own. It proves a pipeline that can run and roll back JCL level jobs, and its secrets scan should catch the clear text login in FTPJCL.JCL. The fences are prerequisites for wave 5 and need no port before then.

waves.name: Read only batch and the import job
waves.rationale: Batch programs that read the account, card, cross reference and customer masters and print them, plus CBIMPORT, which the seed treats as read only because its outputs are private. They share four record copybooks with everything later (CVACT01Y, CVACT02Y, CVACT03Y, CVCUS01Y), so this is where fixed width records and zoned decimal handling get proven. Two caveats. CBIMPORT opens a DD its job never defines (CBIMPORT.cbl:63), so that job cannot run as written. CBACT01C calls an assembler routine, COBDATFT, that needs a replacement (CBACT01C.cbl:231). The wave is sound: nothing shared is written, rollback is discarding output, and the boundary is a file diff.
waves.unblocks: The record layouts and decimal handling that waves 3, 5 and 6 reuse, and the first golden master files, built from the sample data in app/data.

waves.name: Sign on, menus and read only screens
waves.rationale: Online transactions that write nothing another entry point uses. Sign on, main menu and admin menu are one strongly connected component (COSGN00C, COMEN01C, COADM01C) and they route to every online transaction, including those in waves 5, 6 and 7. So the component can move only behind a facade that can still send control to legacy programs by name. The 28 computed calls are mostly bounded by the menu tables (02-coupling.md), but the returns that use CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM are inference. COTRN00C and COTRN01C are a second component. Wave 3 reads masters that legacy batch still writes, so a read path over the legacy VSAM files is needed until wave 5. CORPT00C left this wave (deviation).
waves.unblocks: Retiring the CICS front end screen by screen. After this wave a user can sign on and browse accounts, cards and transactions on the new stack, while every update still runs on the mainframe.

waves.name: Build and demo jobs
waves.rationale: Batch jobs that read datasets other entry points use, through a utility, so the seed cannot tell reads from writes. Seven of the eleven units are mainframe build jobs and procs (samples/jcl, samples/proc) that a new build pipeline replaces. INTRDRJ1 and INTRDRJ2 are an internal reader demo. DEFGDGD defines backup generation bases, and TXT2PDF1 runs a REXX tool that is not in the tree. This is a grab bag, not a wave, and it has no deliverable a stakeholder can name. Retire the build jobs, and handle DEFGDGD and TXT2PDF1 inside wave 5.
waves.unblocks: Nothing. It is a chore. It removes half of the mainframe build path; the other half (CIDBCMP, BLDCIDB2) sits in wave 7.

waves.name: Batch that writes the shared masters
waves.rationale: Batch jobs that write datasets other entry points also use. This holds the daily posting chain (POSTTRAN, TRANBKP, COMBTRAN, TRANIDX, INTCALC), the master reloads (ACCTFILE, CARDFILE, CUSTFILE, XREFFILE, TRANFILE, DISCGRP, TCATBALF, TRANCATG, TRANTYPE, DUSRSECJ), the report and statement pipeline (TRANREPT, CBTRN03C, CREASTMT, CBSTM03A and B, PRTCATBL) and the export. All three must-not-break items live here. Four wrapper scripts run these jobs in fixed orders, and the Control-M folders chain them with high confidence conditions. Joined by deviation: CORPT00C and proc TRANREPT (the online request and the proc of the report), CSUTLDTC (the date routine its first caller now needs) and nine Control-M entries. One sentence describes the wave, so I did not cut it, but at 51 units it is too large to port in one piece, and 03-waves.md gives the order inside it. The unparsed CA-7 listing has job CBPAUP0J, a wave 7 unit, triggering POSTTRAN, so this wave needs a bridge to wave 7 or that trigger has to be re-cut. Until wave 6 ends the shared VSAM masters need a data access facade, because the legacy online writers still use them.
waves.unblocks: Retiring the batch window. After this wave nightly posting, interest, master reloads, the transaction report and statements run on the new stack. It also fixes the record layouts that waves 6 and 7 must honor through the shared masters.

waves.name: Online writers
waves.rationale: Online transactions that write the account, card, transaction and user masters. The seed puts them after the batch writers, which is right: they write the same VSAM files the posting run owns, so the batch side has to be stable first. COCRDLIC and COUSR00C look read only but can reach the update programs by XCTL, so they move with them. COBIL00C assigns a transaction id by reading the last key and adding 1 (COBIL00C.cbl:212-217), a concurrency defect a port must not copy, and it writes the same account balance the posting run writes. Every unit has a computed call, so confidence cannot be high. While any of these programs still writes the legacy masters, wave 5 cannot own them alone.
waves.unblocks: Retiring the CICS regions for account, card, bill payment, transaction and user maintenance, and with them CLOSEFIL, OPENFIL and the CEMT fences.

waves.name: IMS, DB2 and MQ subsystems
waves.rationale: Entry points that touch DB2, IMS or MQ: the card authorization decision (COPAUA0C and its viewers), transaction type maintenance (COTRTLIC, COTRTUPC, COBTUPDT), the IMS unload and load utilities, and the MQ inquiry services (COACCT01, CODATE01). The extractor reads none of the three: DB2 DDL, IMS DBD and PSB files and control cards are all on the not parsed list, so every edge here is a lower bound. CREADB2 joined from wave 1 (deviation). COPAUS0C and COPAUS1C are one component. These need decisions about IMS and MQ targets before they can be sequenced with any confidence.
waves.unblocks: Retiring the last mainframe subsystems, and the IMS and MQ dependency of CBPAUP0J, which triggers POSTTRAN in the CA-7 listing.

unassigned.reason: not reached by any static edge and no job or CSD entry names it. Its DDs are unmapped. The 28 computed calls in reachable programs are bounded by the menu tables and literals (02-coupling.md), which do not name it, but that is inference, so it stays unknown. Ask the client whether anyone runs it by hand.

deviations.reason: Must-not-break item: the transaction report. CORPT00C is the online request that builds JCL text naming EXEC PROC=TRANREPT and writes it to TDQ JOBS, so it is coupled to the wave 5 report pipeline (CBTRN03C, job TRANREPT, proc TRANREPT). Porting it in wave 3 would mean building a job submit bridge to legacy JCL that wave 5 then throws away.

Something the extractor could not see: the proc is named only in JCL text inside CORPT00C, so the seed left it unplaced. It runs SORT and CBTRN03C for the must-not-break transaction report, so it moves with CBTRN03C and job TRANREPT. It stays in the unknown dead code bucket until the client confirms use.

Something the extractor could not see: the steps are IKJEFT01 DB2 utilities (DSNTIAD, DSNTEP4) whose SQL sits in CNTL members, which are on the not-parsed list, so the seed treated the job as touching no DB2. It creates and loads the DB2 transaction type tables, so it moves with the wave 7 DB2 units.

Follow on to moving CORPT00C. The seed moves a subprogram with the earliest family of its callers. Its callers are now CORPT00C (wave 5), COTRN02C (wave 6) and COACTUPC (wave 6), so the earliest is wave 5. Risk rule 4 agrees: risks.json scores it high-high (a date rule that drifts is silently accepted in three programs), and nothing is gained by porting it before a caller can use it.

Dependency: Control-M runs the folder DAILY-TransactionBackup as one sequence, tied by high confidence conditions to the wave 5 job TRANBKP. The seed cut the sequence across waves 1, 2 and 5, and a chain split that way cannot be cut over or rolled back as a unit. The scheduler entry moves to the wave of the last job in its chain. The JCL job it names stays where it is.
